subject.title: fix(kill-tree): verify process group leader before using group kill to prevent gateway SIGTERM (#76259)

question: After rebase, should OpenClaw accept helper-side process-group leader detection as the compatibility fix for omitted-detached Unix cleanup, or require a narrower caller-only replacement?
rationale: The code appears to address the reported gateway SIGTERM bug, but it changes a shared process-tree default and now conflicts with newer process cleanup work, so maintainer intent is needed for the final compatibility shape.

options.title: Rebase and accept this shape
options.body: Resolve conflicts against current main, preserve newer cleanup paths, rerun focused process proof, and land the helper-side leader check if the audit still holds.

options.title: Require caller-only replacement
options.body: Close or supersede this branch with a narrower PR that only forwards actual detachment facts without changing omitted-option helper behavior.

options.title: Pause for process-owner redesign
options.body: Hold the PR until owners define a single canonical process-tree termination contract across agent-core, supervisor, MCP, LSP, shell, and exec paths.

recommendation.title: Rebase and accept this shape
recommendation.body: Resolve conflicts against current main, preserve newer cleanup paths, rerun focused process proof, and land the helper-side leader check if the audit still holds.

likelyOwner.reason: He has recent broad ownership signals across the agent-runtime extraction and adjacent process hardening touched by this compatibility decision.
